senses.gloss:
€1Ā. (भिक्षते, भिक्षित) 
__1 To ask, beg or ask for (with two acc.); भिक्षमाणो वनं प्रियाम् [[Bk. 6. 9.]] 
__2 To beg (as alms); न यज्ञार्थं धनं शूद्राद्विप्रो भिक्षेत कर्हिचित् [[Ms. 11. 24]], 25. 
__3 To ask without obtaining. 
__4 To be weary or distressed. 
__5 To obtain.

[भिक्ष्-अ] 
__1 Asking, begging, soliciting; वृत्ते शराबसंपाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश्चरेत् [[Ms. 6. 56.]] 
__2 Anything given as alms, alms; भवति भिक्षां देहि. 
__3 Wages, hire. 
__4 Service. 
__5 A means of subsistence; अपेतक्लमसंतापाः सुभिक्षाः सुप्रतिश्रयाः [Page1197-2] [[Rām. 2. 92. 6.]] 
-Comp. 
-अटनम् wandering about begging for alms; रुद्रो येन कपालपाणिपुटके भिक्षाटनं कारितः [[Bh. 2. 95.]] 
(-नः) a beggar, mendicant. 
-अन्नम् food obtained by begging, alms. 
-अयनम् (णम्) = भिक्षाटन q. v. 
-अर्थिन् a. begging for alms or charity. (-m.) a beggar. 
-अर्ह a. worthy of alms, a fit object of charity. 
-अशनम् the food obtained by begging; भिक्षाशनं तदपि नीरसमेकबारम् [[Bh. 3. 19.]] 
-आशिन् a. 
__1 living on alms; भिक्षाशी जनमध्यसंगरहितः [[Bh. 3. 86.]] 
__2 dishonest. 
-आहारः begged food; [[Bh. 3. 144.]] 
-उपजीविन् a. living on alms, a beggar. 
-करणम् asking alms, begging. 
-चरः, -चारः a beggar or mendicant. 
-चरणम्, -चर्यम्, -चर्या wandering about begging for alms. 
-पात्रम् a begging-bowl, an alms-dish; so भिक्षाभाण्डम्, भिक्षाभाजनम्. 
-भुज् a. living on alms. 
-माणवः a young beggar (used as a term of contempt); [[P. VI. 2. 69]] com. 
-वासस् n. a beggar's dress. 
-वृत्तिः f. living by begging, a mendicant's life.

[भिक्ष्-उन्] 
__1 A beggar, mendicant in general; भिक्षां च भिक्षबे दद्यात् [[Ms. 3. 94.]] 
__2 A religious mendicant, a Brāhmaṇa in the fourth order of his religious life (when he quits his house and family and lives only on alms), a Sannyāsin. 
__3 The fourth order or stage in the religious life of a Brāhmaṇa (संन्यास). 
__4 A Buddhist mendicant. 
-Comp. 
-चर्या begging, a mendicant's life. 
-भावः monk-hood, priest-hood. 
-सङ्घः a society of Buddhist mendicants. 
-सङ्घाती old or tattered clothes (चीबर). 
-सूत्रम् a collection of rules for mendicants; [[P. IV. 3. 110.]]

[भिक्ष्-उक] A beggar, mendicant; आकीर्णं भिक्षुकैर्बान्यैरगारमुपसंव्रजेत् [[Ms. 6. 51.]] 
-की A female mendicant; cf. भिक्षुणी A Buddhist nun.
